title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
Scammers used a fake AI-generated website to display false account information to a cryptocurrency investor, making fraudulent trading activity appear legitimate on his screen. The victim could see apparent returns on small initial investments and withdrawals, which built confidence before he was asked to commit larger sums. The fake website was the mechanism that sustained the deception through the critical phase when trust was being established.

This was a failure in the user's ability to verify what he was seeing on his own device. No independent confirmation of account balances or transaction history reached him through a separate channel. The scammer's use of an AI-generated website shows how readily such tools can now produce convincing but false interfaces at scale.

It is not established what company operated the legitimate trading app, whether the app itself was compromised, or what steps might have prevented the victim from being directed to the fake website in the first place.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a mobile trading app, gradually building his trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw funds. Over time, Jerry invested increasingly larger amounts, believing he was seeing legitimate returns on his account.

The scheme unraveled when Jerry tried to make a larger withdrawal and discovered he could not access his money. Police determined that while the trading app was real, scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that showed false account information on Jerry's screen. The couple has lost their entire life savings and is warning others about the sophistication of these scams. They are working with Gwinnett County police, though investigators say victims rarely recover stolen funds in these cases. Their children have started a GoFundMe to help them with expenses.
